races.name: Bar 1 Betting Rated Novice Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Tell Us This
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on Good at Tramore giving this horse legitimate course-and-distance claims, but its true style is hold-up and it is likely to find itself racing in a more compressed midfield position than ideal given the cluster of similar types; Conor Stone-Walsh rides for Andrew McNamara whose stable has had a quiet 14-day spell (0/10), and 16 days since last run is fine.

runners_data.name: Cappa Hill
runners_data.note: OR 120 and the pick on official ratings alongside several rivals, but recent form figures of 188-75 are patchy and the horse has struggled at 17-19f on Good previously (five runs, only one win); a natural hold-up horse that faces an awkward positional squeeze with so many similar types in the field, and Sam Ewing will need a good run through traffic.

runners_data.name: Killeemore Lad
runners_data.note: Last ran just nine days ago and returns quickly, which is worth monitoring for freshness, though Andrew Slattery has been in decent form over 14 days (3/32); naturally a hold-up performer, this horse will be shuffled into midfield rather than off the pace as preferred, and Darragh O'Keeffe will need a clear passage — the F in recent form denotes a fall, so jumping confidence is a question mark.

runners_data.name: Luker's Tipple
runners_data.note: The race's key pace-maker and the only runner certain to get its natural position — two consecutive wins over 18f on Good underline both the trip and going suitability, and Gavin Cromwell's horses have been ticking over (1/26 over 14 days); at OR 120 this is a career-high mark but the tactical advantage of uncontested front-running on this track is significant.

runners_data.name: Missus Beeton
runners_data.note: Winless in four runs on Good ground (sim-going score 0W4P) against a record that includes wins on Soft, so the going is a legitimate concern on this surface; Donagh Meyler rides for J P Dempsey, who has had limited runners recently (0/4 over 14 days), and the tp headgear suggests a horse that needs covering up — harder to do in a race where the hold-up berths are all congested.

runners_data.name: Playtime
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old has been running consistently without winning, with form figures of 632736 suggesting a horse that places rather than lands the prize; the trainer has been active and in form (4/49 over 14 days), and Danny Gilligan gets the ride — best Going record of the hold-up group on Good (1W4P) and the second-place finish over 16f on Good is the form to note if the race develops into a late scramble.

races.paceDynamic: Luker's Tipple is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-horse novice chase and, with no rival willing or able to seriously contest the lead, Keith Donoghue can dictate a sustainable, controlled tempo from the front on Good ground at Tramore. The chasing pack — Tell Us This, Cappa Hill, Killeemore Lad, Missus Beeton and Playtime — are all natural hold-up or wait-and-pounce horses, meaning Luker's Tipple faces zero early pressure and can set a pace entirely on its own terms. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can position at the rear, with Killeemore Lad, Cappa Hill and Tell Us This all likely compressed into a midfield cluster rather than settling as true last-to-first runners; Luker's Tipple is the only horse truly certain to get its natural position. This race shape strongly favours the prominent/front-running profile — a lone leader on Good ground over this trip with a quality handler such as Gavin Cromwell is the textbook setup for a front-runner to control and win.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Luker's Tipple Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Luker's Tipple jumps cleanly and is allowed to dictate an uncontested, measured gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: Donoghue sets a rhythm that suits the horse's recent winning form over 18f on Good, and with no rival willing to go with him, the leader banks energy through the middle section before asserting from the final fence.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Luker's Tipple sets a generous early pace that leaves it vulnerable in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: One of the compressed midfield hold-up types gets a golden run through to deliver a late challenge, benefitting from a strong pace having burned off rivals; this shape requires that shape to genuinely materialise from horses whose natural position has been redistributed, making it inherently less likely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jumping Error Reshuffles Race
scenarios.trigger: If Luker's Tipple or another prominent horse makes a costly jumping mistake that resets the race dynamic.
scenarios.body: A fencing incident at a critical point — particularly on Tramore's testing layout — brings the midfield cluster into contention earlier than intended, allowing a horse with a clean round to capitalise; Playtime and Killeemore Lad, both with recent form at this distance on Good, are best placed to benefit from such a reshuffle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Grinds It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally too strong for the distance and conditions tighten into a stamina battle from three fences out.
scenarios.body: Horses with proven staying form on Good ground come to the fore as rivals capitulate; Missus Beeton has winning form at this trip on Soft but her Going record here on Good is weak, while Tell Us This's course-and-distance winning form makes it marginally interesting in this shape despite being redistributed from its true hold-up role.

watchPoints.text: Luker's Tipple's jumping must be tracked from the first fence — any early mistake or jumping hesitation hands the lead to an unlikely rival and collapses the dominant race shape entirely.

The cluster of five hold-up/midfield types is unusually large for a six-runner field; watch the early stages for bumping or crowding as Killeemore Lad, Cappa Hill and Tell Us This all seek similar ground behind the leader.
Killeemore Lad returns on just a nine-day turnaround and had a fall in recent form — if jumping errors recur under Darragh O'Keeffe, it becomes a safety concern as well as a race-shape factor.

Missus Beeton's record on Good ground is a consistent negative (0W4P in similar conditions) — if the going plays fast and true all afternoon, her chance is materially undermined regardless of position in the race.

Playtime's trainer Elliott has four winners from 49 runners over the past 14 days — form in the yard is live, and if the pace collapses or a reshuffle occurs, this horse's consistency around 16-17f on Good makes it a logical beneficiary.

races.name: O'Neill's Bar Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Burru
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has placed twice on Good ground recently; the Tiernan Power Roche booking adds confidence, 80 days off is notable but sim-going figures (15/15 Good) suggest the surface is no barrier, and tracking Le Kap from second should suit.

runners_data.name: Coded Welder
runners_data.note: Fitted with a tongue-tie, Danny Gilligan takes the ride for the improving Cian Collins yard who are 1/15 in the last 14 days; placed on Good four times, this 7-year-old's consistent form figures suggest he handles this sort of flat track and should press for the lead from the outset.

runners_data.name: Frankie's Freebie
runners_data.note: Harry Sexton claims 7lbs for his father Adrian, keeping costs down on a horse that has finished second twice at this sort of trip on Good; the combination of claim and familiarity with the horse is an obvious angle, though the sim-going win rate (0 wins from 9) is a soft flag.

runners_data.name: Happy Me
runners_data.note: W J Burke's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse at heart — its best form comes from off the pace — but with this field stacked with closers, it will be pressed into a more prominent position than ideal, making it harder to produce its natural finish; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) reflects that constraint.

runners_data.name: Juke Hill
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends a 6-year-old fitted with a hood for the first time; the trainer's recent strike rate (4/49) provides context, and Juke Hill's form reads as a horse still finding its feet over fences, but it has the class ceiling to be competitive if the late run materialises.

runners_data.name: Le Kap
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's tongue-tied six-year-old is the confirmed pace-setter here and will enjoy an uncontested lead on Good ground; the absence of wins on Good (0/5 sim-going) is worth noting, and the STYLE_FIT tag suggests it may not always get the run of things, but today it dictates.

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old fitted with a visor and just 9 days since last run; Gerard Keane's horse is a true hold-up type by profile but will find it difficult to settle into its natural position from the rear in this field, with the redistribution meaning it races out of role — the STYLE_FIT discount (0.92) applies.

runners_data.name: Rattledelatch
runners_data.note: John Queally's five-year-old carries a clear finishing tendency flag — fades late — which is a significant liability over 2m6f on a track where stamina will be tested; form figures (P0-960) are uninspiring and there is no headgear change to spark improvement.

runners_data.name: Kasper Hauser
runners_data.note: The youngest in the field at four, this horse arrives on the back of a win 20 days ago and has the most solid recent form of any hold-up type here (52-531); Calum Hogan's 5lb claim helps under top weight of 154lbs, and the horse's pattern of closing from mid-division makes it the most credible late challenger.

races.paceDynamic: Le Kap is the one confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner beginners' chase and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested gallop on Good ground over 2m6f at Tramore. The pace will be sustainable rather than searching, which historically suits prominent-to-midfield horses who can travel within themselves before picking off a tiring leader in the final circuit. Happy Me and Mephisto are genuine hold-up types by profile but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because this field contains more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Le Kap and the prominent trio of Burru, Coded Welder, and Frankie's Freebie are best placed to dictate their natural positions. With one honest, unpressured pace-setter setting a steady tempo, this race shape most favours prominent-to-midfield horses with stamina to grind through the final mile — horses that can track Le Kap closely and produce a sustained run rather than a late sprint.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Le Kap controls from the front at a fair but uncontested tempo and prominent chasers sit just behind throughout.
scenarios.body: Le Kap sets a genuine rhythm that strings the field out over 2m6f, and the horses tracking in second or third are best placed to challenge as the leader's stamina is tested late on Good ground. Prominent runners with course-distance stamina who can travel economically behind the leader are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Le Kap Steals It Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Le Kap's uncontested lead evolves into a race-long advantage that the field never seriously threatens.
scenarios.body: Racing on the front end with no pressure, Le Kap is able to control the pace, conserve energy over the fences, and simply refuse to be caught once jumping accurately through the final circuit. This is most plausible if the prominent horses are slow to exert pressure or if jumping errors disrupt the chasers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final half-mile and a horse from behind the midfield pack produces a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Kasper Hauser, who has a recent win and credible form figures, has the profile to make ground if the race develops a strong enough gallop to soften those in front; Juke Hill from the Elliott yard could also emerge with a fresh enough run. The scenario is discounted because Happy Me and Mephisto — the redistirbuted true hold-up types — will struggle to access their natural closing position and are rated at a style-fit discount.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or scrimmaging disrupts the lead group and turns this into a ragged, stop-start contest.
scenarios.body: In a beginners' chase over 2m6f, inexperienced jumpers can unsettle the race shape entirely; any big error from Le Kap would remove the pace anchor and leave the field bunched with no obvious organiser. Rattledelatch's tendency to fade in the finish makes it a loser in this shape, while a horse like Juke Hill with a hold-up profile could capitalise on the ensuing confusion.

watchPoints.text: Le Kap's jumping accuracy is critical — if Darragh O'Keeffe's mount makes a serious error at any of the early fences, the entire race shape collapses and the field loses its pace anchor entirely.

Happy Me and Mephisto are both genuine hold-up types who will be forced closer to the pace than suits them; watch for either horse being caught in traffic or unable to produce their natural finish, which is a key reason to discount them.

Rattledelatch's stamina fade flag is significant at 2m6f — watch if Ian Power asks it to be prominent early, as a weakening jumper in a beginners' chase creates danger for others at the fences in the home straight.

Kasper Hauser is the one hold-up horse whose recent form justifies monitoring for a late move; if the pace is honest enough to set up a closing run, this four-year-old with a recent win is the one to track from halfway.

Coded Welder's tongue-tie fitting and the live Cian Collins yard (1/15 in 14 days) is a small but concrete angle — watch if Danny Gilligan takes a lead on Le Kap from an early stage rather than sitting back, which would tighten the scenario considerably.

races.name: McDonald & Son Builders Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Johnny Rambo
runners_data.note: Prominent-running 4yo with a win and a place on Good ground (both at similar trip), trained by Donncha Duggan; 10 days since last run, consistent in this going, and ideally drawn to track the leader from the front rank without overextending.

runners_data.name: Devine Genius
runners_data.note: Carries headgear (t) and has a fade-in-finish flag; naturally a hold-up type but redistributed to mapped midfield because the field's rear is congested — true style is further back, which diminishes its appeal in a pace-controlled single-leader scenario.

runners_data.name: Folk Warrior
runners_data.note: A genuine rear-division operator pushed forward on the map due to redistribution; poor recent form across varying surfaces (8th on Good, 5th on Standard) and a 5-day turnaround makes this look like a tentative entry in search of easier company.

runners_data.name: Green Grass
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a fade flag and only one run under the belt (13th on Good over 19f); trainer Paul Flynn has had no winners in 14 days from 20 runners, and this profile asks many questions for a maiden hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: I'm All In
runners_data.note: Prominent style with Gordon Elliott and Sam Ewing; returned U-U before a 9th last time, so reliability is a concern, but the prominent position over 2m Good should suit physically if jumping holds up — the Elliott yard has had four winners in 14 days from 49 runners.

runners_data.name: John Gun
runners_data.note: Unknown style and lightly raced with no form string or last run date supplied; Kieran Purcell yard quiet (0/1 in 14 days), making this a near-complete unknown quantity — must be treated cautiously in scenario planning.

runners_data.name: Pinkarizon
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with headgear (t) and a string of pulled-up or mid-division finishes in Good-ground maidens; Liam McKenna's 3lb claim helps, but the pace dynamic here offers no obvious late window for a horse with this profile.

runners_data.name: Spanish Rising
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's 4yo carries the quality stable flag and has been placed once (4th on Good, 18f), showing some affinity with this trip and going; a true hold-up type who showed his best Flat form at 10f, suggesting stamina is developing.

runners_data.name: Faerie Tales
runners_data.note: Paul Fahey's 4yo is a natural hold-up horse with a consistent fade flag; bumped to mapped midfield due to redistribution — all four form runs ended 12th or worse, all on Good, and the 33-day break adds uncertainty despite the 7lb claim.

runners_data.name: Noble Rocco
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from the Gordon Elliott yard with two hurdling runs both in the 7-9 bracket on Good ground; 32 days since last run, no wins or places, but the yard's recent form (4/49 in 14 days) gives minor yard confidence without making this an obvious profile match.

runners_data.name: Really Truly
runners_data.note: Lightly raced unknown with J J Slevin booked — that's the headline, as the Joseph Patrick O'Brien yard has been in strong form (7/61 in 14 days); headgear (h) listed, unknown going preference, but Slevin's booking in a maiden with an unraced type from a powerful stable demands respect.

runners_data.name: Rosarian
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner in the race, ridden by Danny Mullins; has form of a 2nd on Good over 19f and a 7th on Yielding, so the going suits — maps as the pace controller and is the axis around which all scenarios revolve, with a slight style-fit discount already applied.

races.paceDynamic: Rosarian is the one confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner maiden hurdle and, with Danny Mullins aboard, will stride onto the lead from the off over Tramore's right-handed 2m trip on Good ground. The pace will be honest but controlled — Rosarian is not being pressured by a rival of similar speed, meaning the tempo is likely to suit a horse travelling well just off the leader rather than a late finisher. Johnny Rambo and I'm All In are mapped prominent and will track Rosarian closely, keeping the gallop honest without turning it into a true test. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit within a length or two of the pace and pounce from the front of the pack; true hold-up types face an uphill task as the modest-pace single-leader scenario rarely generates the late acceleration window they need. The field contains more genuine hold-up horses than the map can place at the rear — Faerie Tales, Devine Genius, and Folk Warrior are redistributed to midfield but are true closers who will likely find themselves further back than ideal in this controlled-pace scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rosarian Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Rosarian is allowed to dictate a comfortable gallop unchallenged, the race is run to suit horses racing prominently just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Rosarian sets a sustainable tempo through the middle stages and the race becomes a test of jumping accuracy and staying power over the final two flights; horses positioned second or third with minimal fuss will be perfectly placed to strike as Rosarian tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Duo Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses (Rosarian, Johnny Rambo) go clear together and the field strings out early, the race becomes a two-horse battle from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A moderate gallop with limited pressure from behind allows the lead pair to build an unassailable advantage; any horse further back in midfield will find the margin impossible to make up in 2m on Good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop proves faster than expected and the front pair burn each other out before the last, a well-positioned midfield horse can pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Spanish Rising and Really Truly, both carrying quality hints, could benefit if they travel smoothly in midfield and find room on the home turn; Tramore's run-in is short, so this requires a perfect position entering the straight, not a true hold-up run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Deliver Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely strong from the outset and the front-runners capitulate, a redistributed hold-up type could produce a late run.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given Rosarian's one-dimensional lead role and the absence of a pace partner to force a burn-up; Faerie Tales or Devine Genius would need conditions materially different from what the pace data implies.

watchPoints.text: Rosarian's jumping must be tracked from the first flight — if Danny Mullins establishes a clear lead without jumping errors, the race shape locks in and prominent racers Johnny Rambo and I'm All In become the primary dangers.

Really Truly is an unknown quantity with J J Slevin booked for Joseph Patrick O'Brien and headgear applied on debut — if this horse breaks quickly and travels well, it could upend the projected order significantly.

The redistribution cluster (Faerie Tales, Devine Genius, Folk Warrior) risks creating a congested mid-pack in the early stages on Tramore's tight track — watch for traffic issues or interference between the 1st and 3rd hurdles.

Green Grass and I'm All In both carry fade-in-finish flags over 2m on Good; if either runner begins to weaken from the second-last, they could impede horses tracking them through the home turn — Tramore's short run-in amplifies this risk.

Trainer 14-day form for Paul W Flynn (0/20) and T:J Morrison (0/2) flags stables in poor recent form; if their runners (Green Grass, Devine Genius) drift or show signs of unreadiness in the paddock, the market may offer a reliable directional signal.

races.name: Flynn Hotel Group Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Churchwarden
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's six-year-old has form figures of 1 and 2 at 12f on Good, handles this going well across nine similar-ground runs (2 wins, 4 places), and wears a hood; returning after 37 days, this is a natural closer who should be racing deepest of all, giving him every chance if the pace softens late.|

runners_data.name: Palace Boy
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran fresh off a 10-day turnaround with Donoghue aboard; his Good-ground record shows just one place from four runs at this distance range and the trainer's yard is cold at 0/1 over 14 days — his hold-up profile asks for a pace collapse that this shape may not deliver.|

runners_data.name: Dairy Force
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and sole pace-setter in the field; Elliott's seven-year-old has finished in the frame in four of her last five starts on Good ground and wears headgear, though the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 flags she is not a natural front-runner — if she finds the front role uncomfortable she could weaken from two out.|

runners_data.name: Claude
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a modest recent form string (7P-030) and a genuine hold-up profile that has been remapped toward midfield given the volume of closers in this field — Connell's yard has no runners in the past 14 days, and the horse's ten Good-ground runs have produced only one win, limiting confidence in a forward move.|

runners_data.name: Rightfolksplease
runners_data.note: Queally's eight-year-old carries the best similar-going strike rate in the field (13 runs, 2 wins, 6 places on Good) and was seen five days ago, suggesting freshness is not a concern; though a true hold-up horse shuffled forward on the map, if he can settle handy in third he has the class to threaten — the 7lb claim from Healy is a useful weight aid.|

runners_data.name: Kome Dans Un Reve
runners_data.note: Fenton's six-year-old returns from a 78-day absence wearing no headgear, with a fade-in-finish warning flag and a similar-going record of 0 wins from 5 runs — the redistribution to midfield masks a hold-up horse who typically weakens rather than stays on, making this the most vulnerable runner in the field if the pace is steady.|

races.paceDynamic: Dairy Force is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to push her, she should be able to dictate a sustainable, controlled tempo from the front over the 2m trip on Good ground at Tramore. Behind her, the field is dominated by hold-up types — Churchwarden, Palace Boy, Claude, Rightfolksplease, and Kome Dans Un Reve all want to race off the pace — meaning the race shape is unusually clear: one horse leads, the rest follow at a distance. This field holds more hold-up types than can all occupy their natural position; Claude and Rightfolksplease are remapped to midfield, but Churchwarden and Palace Boy are the truest closers and most likely to settle deepest. A lone, uncontested front-runner on Good ground setting a manageable gallop strongly favours a horse who can travel close to the pace or produce a well-timed kick — pure hold-up horses arriving late will need the tempo to collapse, and with Dairy Force setting a metronomic rather than punishing pace, that scenario looks unlikely.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dairy Force Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Dairy Force leads unchallenged and sets a fair but sustainable tempo, allowing her to conserve energy and repel rivals.
scenarios.body: Dairy Force dictates from the front without a yard of pressure, likely quickening modestly from two out over this flat-ish track; her Good-ground form is solid and Gordon Elliott's yard is in decent nick at 4/49 over the past 14 days. Any horse that can travel in second or third — most naturally Rightfolksplease or Churchwarden on a good day — needs to close a controlled gap, which suits a winner who can sustain rather than sprint.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace slackens into the home straight, causing the field to bunch and creating a sprint finish that genuine closers can exploit.
scenarios.body: Churchwarden or Palace Boy, racing deepest from an off-the-pace position, would benefit most if Dairy Force ties up or misjudges the tempo in the final two hurdles; Churchwarden has course-distance form on Good and is trained by De Bromhead who places horses well. Palace Boy is 10 days fresh, carries some form on Good and with Donoghue in the saddle has the experience to deliver late if a gap appears.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Picks Up
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a two-paced affair with a brief injection of pace from three out, triggering a scramble where the remapped midfield horses get involved.
scenarios.body: Rightfolksplease, who has genuine class-level form at 16f on Good (two wins, six places in similar going over 15 outings), could find herself ideally positioned between the leader and the backmarkers if she settles in third; Claude showed a placed effort at 17f on Good and with a clean round could make the frame. However, both are tagged as true hold-up horses mapped forward, and their style fit is discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Dairy Force goes off too hard or makes a jumping error and the race falls apart, leaving it wide open for anything to grab it.
scenarios.body: Kome Dans Un Reve has a notable fade-in-finish flag and 78 days off the track, making her an unlikely beneficiary even in a messy race; however, a field-wide scramble could theoretically hand the race to any survivor. This remains the lowest-probability outcome given the steady Good ground and the lack of any horse likely to push Dairy Force into a suicidal gallop.

watchPoints.text: Dairy Force's jumping must be monitored — any error at a hurdle from the front could unsettle her rhythm and unravel the entire pace map, gifting the race to Churchwarden or Palace Boy.

Rightfolksplease ran only five days ago; if the quick turnaround leaves him flat in the closing stages, the midfield position he is mapped to could leave him stranded between the pace and the closers.

Kome Dans Un Reve's 78-day layoff combined with his fade-in-finish flag makes him a significant drifting risk in-running — if he weakens from two out he could cause interference for horses travelling behind.
Churchwarden's headgear (hood) and De Bromhead's positive 14-day record (4/37) are worth tracking in the market — any market support from a yard known for placing horses sharply should be noted.
The Good ground has been consistent across all seven Tramore races today, meaning no unexpected surface variance is likely to disadvantage or assist any runner disproportionately.

races.name: WTW Willis Rated Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Early Dawning
runners_data.note: Won over this trip on Good at Leopardstown last time out (28 days ago), Mullins/Mullins combination is always significant, and a prominent style that should see him track Master Haku comfortably — conditions and distance suit well.|

runners_data.name: Mr Master Mac
runners_data.note: Boasts a strong record in similar going (6 runs, 2 wins, 5 places) and has course experience at this trip; Thomas O'Connor's 7lb claim is useful, though trainer Fahey is in quiet form (0/7 in past 14 days), and he will want to sit close to the pace throughout.|

runners_data.name: Siege Of Carthage
runners_data.note: Hold-up style operated by Slevin who is adept at timing a late run, but a slow early gallop is his enemy; won over 20f on Good and placed at 18f in Heavy, so the trip and going are not concerns — it is race shape rather than ability that is the obstacle.|

runners_data.name: Master Haku
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the field, Gordon Elliott-trained, with two wins and three places in six Good-ground starts; Sam Ewing gets the ride on a horse who showed at Punchestown last time (1st, 20f, Good) that he can dominate when allowed to bowl along — this race sets up perfectly for him.|

runners_data.name: Lureka Du Noyer
runners_data.note: De Bromhead yard has had recent winners (4/37 in 14 days) and Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong booking; Lureka won over 16f on Good and followed up over 18f, stepping up to 20f here for the first time, and the tongue-tie is noted — likely to be prominent but may find the extra distance an unknown quantity.|

runners_data.name: Holy Joe
runners_data.note: Two consecutive wins on Good ground (20f and 16f) make him a form player, and Elliott runs two today suggesting stable confidence; a hold-up horse who needs something to happen in front of him, and in a race likely to be run at a steady tempo that is a significant tactical disadvantage.|

runners_data.name: Butch Coolidge
runners_data.note: Won over 22f on Good ground and is a naturally prominent-running horse by style; at OR 102 he is the lowest-rated runner in this field, and because the race already has multiple prominent types, he is likely to race further back than suits him — STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 signals his chance is tempered by positional compromise rather than ability alone.|

races.paceDynamic: Master Haku is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to press him from the outset, he should secure an uncontested lead at his own tempo over the 2m4½f trip on Good ground at Tramore. Early Dawning, Mr Master Mac, and Lureka Du Noyer are all prominent-types who will want to sit just off the pace rather than challenge him for the lead, creating a controlled, single-file gallop that is unlikely to be truly searching. That moderate, sustainable tempo rewards horses with a tactical turn of foot in the straight rather than relentless stayers, pointing this race shape squarely towards prominent runners who can travel close to the pace and produce a clean jump at the last — rather than hold-up horses forced to make up significant ground late. This field contains more prominent/front-running types than the race can accommodate at the head of affairs: Master Haku is best placed to dictate, with Early Dawning and Mr Master Mac the likeliest to occupy the next positions, while Butch Coolidge, a natural prominent racer, is likely to find himself racing further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Master Haku Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Master Haku bowls along uncontested, sets a fair gallop and finds enough at his hurdles to hold on.
scenarios.body: Master Haku dictates at his own pace from flag to finish, and with no horse willing to close the gap on him through the race, he arrives at the last with reserves intact; his Good-ground form (2W3P in similar conditions) underlines his suitability to exactly this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pegs Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and a prominent racer stalks Master Haku before pouncing from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Early Dawning or Mr Master Mac, travelling smoothly in Master Haku's slipstream, produces a sharper jump at the penultimate hurdle and edges ahead on the run-in; both carry strong Good-ground credentials and the trip looks well within range for either.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely quick enough to string the field out and a hold-up horse picks up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Holy Joe or Siege Of Carthage, held off the pace, would need the leaders to have gone hard enough to come back to them; Holy Joe's two recent wins on Good ground give him a live chance if the tempo is faster than anticipated, though at Tramore a slow-run race makes this profile a tough ask.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Collapses, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If multiple leaders make errors or tire badly and an unfancied runner seizes a vacuum.
scenarios.body: A messy jumping contest that produces multiple casualties or blunders could open the door for Butch Coolidge, who at OR 102 is racing out of his comfort zone positionally but did win over 22f on Good ground; this scenario is unlikely given the small field and experienced jockeys.

watchPoints.text: Master Haku — if he jumps fluently at the first two hurdles and is not pressured, he could build an uncatchable lead; watch his jumping from the off as any mistake could flip the race shape entirely.

Lureka Du Noyer — stepping up in trip for the first time to 20f with a tongue-tie applied; if she struggles to travel at the longer distance, De Bromhead and O'Keeffe may find her weakening later than expected.

Butch Coolidge — a natural front-runner who will likely be shuffled back in a field full of prominent types; watch whether Brian Hayes attempts to push forward early or accepts a rear position, as either decision significantly changes his chance.

Holy Joe — connections of the other Elliott runner; if the stable has a preference between Master Haku and Holy Joe, any market drift on Holy Joe early should be noted as it would reinforce Master Haku as the yard's leading hope.

Going confirmation at race time — all seven races at Tramore today are returning Good, but as the evening progresses and ground is covered, any late softening reported after the 6:48 race could marginally help hold-up horses like Siege Of Carthage and Holy Joe.

races.name: Bluegrass Horse Feeds Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Double Power
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a consistent style who handles good ground (5 from 7 sim-going), though his fade-in-finish flag is a concern over this stiff 2m4½f — he needs the pace to stay honest but not too searching; Keith Donoghue takes the ride for his father's yard in solid 2/11 14-day form.

runners_data.name: Pure Logic
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner who will control tempo unchallenged; Danny Mullins a major positive, but Pure Logic's STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reminds that this lead role is a slight positional stretch, and his 11 placed runs from 12 on similar going suggest he keeps finding one better.

runners_data.name: Diamond Secret
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly, 28 days since last run, handled good ground 5 from 7 times; Philip Fenton's yard has minimal recent firepower (0/1 in 14 days), and she will need to weave through a dense late pack to get a blow at the leaders.

runners_data.name: Arctic Piper
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who settles at the back and requires a stronger pace than Pure Logic is likely to set; poor sim-going record (8 from 14, 0 wins, 1 place) and a form string featuring two pulled-ups make this a hard race to visualise him winning.

runners_data.name: Inchidaly Copper
runners_data.note: The most consistent horse in the race on good ground (14 from 15 sim-going, 3 wins, 7 places), with a solid each-way profile at OR 92; Luke Burke Ott claims 7lb, and while he is a hold-up type who will race closer than ideal given the overcrowded rear, his course-suitable form makes him the most interesting deeper runner.

runners_data.name: Maxicourt
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type with modest form figures but a placed run (3rd) on good ground over similar trip 10 days ago; Daniel King partners a horse who has placed 2 times from 15 on sim-going, suggesting modest each-way claims at best.

runners_data.name: Nashville Notions
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose true racing style means he is forced closer to the pace than suits in this shape — 1 win and 1 place from 12 on sim-going, and a 21-day break; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) confirms the mismatch.

runners_data.name: Taketwotoone
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a fade-in-finish flag who posts very poor form on good ground (0 wins, 0 places from 3 similar-going runs); displaced towards midfield by the crowded rear, the combination of wrong position and wrong ground record makes his task extremely difficult.

runners_data.name: Jack Inthe Jukebox
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing six-year-old who has been off 78 days and returns with hood and tongue-tie from a Flavin yard in quiet form (0/2 in 14 days); form figures include several pulled-ups, but his natural position just off Pure Logic is an asset if fitness is right.

runners_data.name: Miss Guiry
runners_data.note: 266 days off the track is the defining factor here for the five-year-old; genuinely hold-up in style but squeezed forward by the crowded rear, the fade flag and a string of zeros in recent form (0U000) suggest she is a tough ride back to form.

runners_data.name: The Ducks Walk
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old back after 59 days; among the natural hold-up types pushed towards midfield by the field shape, he has placed 4th twice on good ground from just 4 runs, so the trip (2m4½f) at least suits, but he needs a different kind of race to land it.

runners_data.name: Keep The Head
runners_data.note: Veteran at OR 81 who has faded in finishes repeatedly (P9P-P0), carrying the additional burden of the fade flag and a crowded map position; Hanlon's yard (0/20 in 14 days) gives no confidence, and good ground form is poor.

runners_data.name: Talas Kera
runners_data.note: The 24f trip appears within range (4th at 24f on good ground in last 5), and the five-year-old has placed once on similar going from 10 runs; a hold-up type shunted towards midfield, Eoghan Finegan claims 5lb, but the 0 win record is a significant caveat.

runners_data.name: Princess Felicia
runners_data.note: 315 days since last run is an enormous concern for the seven-year-old, who has a placed record (1 from 7 on sim-going) and must overcome a long layoff in a 19-runner field where hold-up types are already fighting for position.

runners_data.name: The Cobblers Wife
runners_data.note: 92 days since last run for Alan O'Sullivan's partner; forced closer than her natural hold-up style demands, and a sim-going record of just 2 from 8 with no wins tells the story of a horse who struggles to convert.

runners_data.name: Youknowme
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a consistent 7th-range form line, fade-in-finish flag, and poor sim-going record (0 wins, 0 places from 8); genuinely a hold-up horse sitting closer than ideal, and the tongue-tie is already fitted — little angle here.

runners_data.name: Lanzhou
runners_data.note: 90 days off the track, Flavin yard quiet (0/2 in 14 days), fade-in-finish flag, and a form string reading 0009-0 with a sim-going record of 2 from 5 and no wins; hold-up style is further diluted by the cramped map, making a big run hard to construct.

runners_data.name: Colesberg
runners_data.note: Top OR in the lower-rated cluster at 93, with only 4 runs in the book; form figures (996-7) are consistent but well beaten, good ground record is just 1 from 4, and no jockey listed raises a practical query — needs a significant improvement on those figures.

runners_data.name: Beacon Bypass
runners_data.note: Four-year-old, 74 days off, a genuine hold-up type that is mapped closer than ideal due to the overcrowded rear; 0 wins and 0 places from 4 sim-going runs, fade-in-finish flag, and the STYLE_FIT discount (0.90) stack up as negatives.

races.paceDynamic: Pure Logic is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, Danny Mullins can control tempo from the front on his own terms over 2m4½f on good ground at Tramore. The pace is unlikely to be searingly fast — a single leader dictating on good ground over this trip typically sets a measured gallop that rewards horses who travel prominently and can sustain their effort into the straight, rather than those held up in the rear who need the race to be run at a searching clip to bring them into it late. Double Power and Jack In The Jukebox are the natural prominent companions who should sit just behind Pure Logic and receive a ground-saving, low-pressure trip, giving prominent-to-midfield travellers with stamina the clearest tactical advantage. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race in the first half of the field, travel comfortably through the race, and hit the front between the last two flights — the field holds significantly more hold-up types than can be accommodated at the rear, with Taketwotoone, Nashville Notions, Beacon Bypass and Miss Guiry among the genuine closers who will be forced to race much closer to the pace than ideal, diluting their chance of delivering a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pure Logic Dictates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Logic is allowed to bowl along at his own pace and the prominent horses behind lack the class to reel him in.
scenarios.body: Pure Logic sets a fair but not punishing gallop with Danny Mullins dictating every yard; any horse who tracks him closely will need to be good enough to go past, but a measured tempo means the lead is never surrendered under pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Double Power or Jack In The Jukebox travel powerfully in Pure Logic's slipstream and find enough to collar him in the final flight.
scenarios.body: A controlled early gallop leaves Pure Logic vulnerable to a horse who has been saved fractionally more ground in second or third; the good going and 2m4½f trip rewards stamina without needing a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Aids Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the leader overcooks it or the field bunches and a strong-finishing hold-up horse finds a gap between the last two hurdles.
scenarios.body: Unlikely given the single-leader shape, but if Pure Logic goes too fast for his own good on a track that turns sharply, a horse with fresh legs from the rear could make up ground; Inchidaly Copper's consistent placed form in similar conditions makes him the prime candidate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Thins Field
scenarios.trigger: If the big field causes interference, a spate of errors or unseated riders, and the race becomes a slog for the few standing.
scenarios.body: A 19-runner handicap hurdle on good ground with a large contingent of hold-up horses forced forward creates congestion and fall risk; a robust, adaptable horse who jumps cleanly and handles traffic survives best.

watchPoints.text: Pure Logic (Danny Mullins) will set the pace entirely alone — watch whether Mullins elects to quicken or sit and if the gallop is too steady it could set up a sprint finish that suits the prominent horses directly behind him.

Double Power carries a fade-in-finish flag and is asked to see out 2m4½f on good ground — if he weakens between the last two hurdles he could take out rival ground from Jack In The Jukebox and compress the field dangerously in a 19-runner race.

The 19-runner field with the majority of horses crammed into midfield creates a significant bunching risk at early hurdles — watch for traffic trouble, particularly for Inchidaly Copper, who needs clean air to make his consistent placed form count.

Inchidaly Copper's 14-from-15 good-ground record is the standout stat in the race — if Luke Burke Ott (7lb claimer) can navigate him to a clear run from the rear-midfield pack, his consistency on this surface makes him a benchmark for assessing others' finishing efforts.

Three Flavin-trained runners (Jack In The Jukebox, Lanzhou, Colesberg) appear with the yard at 0/2 in the last 14 days and two of them returning after 90-day absences — worth monitoring market moves for any sign one is significantly better fancied than the others heading into the race.

races.name: Conor Lannen Country Store (Ladies) Maiden

runners_data.name: Silas Marner
runners_data.note: Trainer Sabrina Harty sends this veteran 9yo out 15 days after his last run with 0W1P from 11 similar-going starts; at his best a hold-up horse, he finds the rear positions crowded and is likely to race closer than ideal, which compromises his typical late-running threat.

runners_data.name: Blue Nasturtium
runners_data.note: A lightly raced 4yo for K J Condon whose only run produced a fourth on good turf — one run of form data leaves her deeply unknown, and the step to 2m without experience of staying this trip is a significant query.

runners_data.name: Dream On Baby
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins's 6yo is the lone front-runner in the field and has been ridden in front or close to the pace throughout recent starts, finishing second three times; with no rival to press her she can set a comfortable gallop and is the pivotal horse in how this race is shaped.

runners_data.name: Fraher Field
runners_data.note: Carries a strong record of placed efforts at 2m on good ground for the Kiely yard; a natural prominent racer who should sit directly behind Dream On Baby and is well placed if the front-runner fades — 10 days since last run is a fresh enough return.

runners_data.name: Goodie Girl
runners_data.note: Three career wins on good turf for Dermot McLoughlin and an ability to stay distances around 2m make her a legitimate runner if conditions suit; the 61-day absence is the principal concern, and she comes from behind so needs others to do the work.

runners_data.name: Kimy
runners_data.note: Thomas Mullins's 6yo tends to fade in the finish and her last five runs show no win and limited placed efforts over distances shorter than this — she is a genuine hold-up type nudged into midfield by the crowded rear, meaning her real style cannot fully express itself in this shape.

runners_data.name: Ma Belle Etoile
runners_data.note: De Bromhead sends her out just 6 days after a run, which demands attention for a yard operating well (T14:4/37); she races prominently and has placed form at 2m on good ground, positioning her as a realistic track-the-leader type.

runners_data.name: Paul's Dream
runners_data.note: Anthony Mullins's 7yo has four wins and eight placed efforts from 12 similar-going runs and boasts wins over 2m and further on good turf — she slots naturally into the prominent group and her record suggests she is the most accomplished horse in the race on raw form.

runners_data.name: Run For Mahler
runners_data.note: Has a win over 2m on good ground and three career wins from staying efforts; raced most recently at shorter and steps back up in trip, and the headgear (tongue-tie) is retained — a hold-up type who needs a strong pace to produce her best.

runners_data.name: Splashing Out
runners_data.note: Multiple wins on good turf including over staying trips, tongue-tie retained, and just 6 days since last run for Eoin Griffin; a hold-up type with a variable record (18th last time) but proven winning ability at the level when conditions fall right.

runners_data.name: Thisistheway
runners_data.note: Yvonne Latta's 7yo has three wins and a consistent record of finishing in the front two on good ground at distances around 2m; races prominently and is well suited to tracking the pace, making her a natural fit if Dream On Baby sets things up from the front.

races.paceDynamic: Dream On Baby is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will stride comfortably to the front from the off and control tempo on her own terms over Tramore's 2m flat circuit. The pace will be honest but uncontested, meaning she dictates every yard and can conserve enough to sustain her effort into the straight — her form string of 222-3 shows she consistently finishes in the places when allowed to bowl along. Behind her, Fraher Field, Ma Belle Etoile, Paul's Dream and Thisistheway are the natural prominent types who will jostle for the three or four berths just off the leader, creating a defined and organised pack through the middle stages. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Dream On Baby at a controlled clip and pounce in the straight, rather than true hold-up horses — and this field holds more hold-up types than the rear positions can accommodate: Silas Marner and Kimy, both genuine closers, have been redistributed to midfield because the map is full at the back, meaning their true style is unlikely to materialise and they should be discounted in shapes that require a late, deep-field run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dream On Baby Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dream On Baby is allowed to lead without any rival willing to press her early and the prominent pack settles into a rhythm behind.
scenarios.body: She controls tempo precisely, conserves energy through the middle circuit and has enough left to hold on as the closers arrive late; her consistent placed form on good turf at this trip makes her the central figure in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting second or third throughout tracks Dream On Baby economically and pounces with a decisive move in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Paul's Dream's outstanding placed and winning record at 2m on good ground makes her ideally suited to this position, while Thisistheway's knack of finishing strongly from just off the pace means she also profits in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Stayer Triumphs
scenarios.trigger: If Dream On Baby's solo lead proves unsustainably strong early and she ties up turning for home, leaving the race open.
scenarios.body: Goodie Girl, with three wins on good turf and a proven ability to stay, could pick up the pieces if the front ends of the field come back to the pack; Splashing Out similarly has multiple wins and could benefit if fatigue reshapes the finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If, against the race-shape expectation, a displaced hold-up type manages to find a clear run late and the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a closing burst.
scenarios.body: This is the lowest-probability shape because the truest closers, Silas Marner and Kimy, are racing out of their natural role and the pace from a single front-runner is unlikely to generate the sustained gallop that pure hold-up types need; both carry discounted chances accordingly.

watchPoints.text: Dream On Baby is completely uncontested for the lead — watch whether Miss O'Sullivan elects to exploit that freedom or is forced wide early by the 11-runner field, as either outcome shapes every other runner's race.

Paul's Dream's trainer Anthony Mullins has a relatively quiet recent strike rate (T14:0/5) despite the horse's outstanding form profile — watch for any market drift that signals connections are not expecting a peak run.

Ma Belle Etoile is running just 6 days after her last start for a trainer firing at 4/37 over 14 days — watch the market closely for support, as short-turnaround runners from form yards in this field are worth monitoring.

Silas Marner and Kimy are both genuine hold-up types but are mapped ahead of their natural position because the rear is over-subscribed — watch early to see whether either horse drops back naturally, which would be positive for their chance, or gets shuffled into a compromised midfield spot.

Splashing Out's form is wildly inconsistent (1st, 18th, 1st in recent starts) — watch how she travels in the early stages, as her tongue-tie and erratic profile mean she is either on a going day or not.
